goals: Mechanistic: characterize how snow accumulation/melt and water partitioning (ET vs runoff vs drainage) vary across the Upper Yakima elevation gradient and soil texture
Validation: compare simulated peak SWE to SNOTEL; assess streamflow against USGS gauges (feasibility-limited)
key_processes: ET / surface runoff / sub-surface drainage partitioning

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM with NLDAS-2 forcing resolves elevation-dependent snow/precip across 1900 m of relief and per-column SSURGO soil; both requested drivers map to available levers.

answerable: Elevation control on snow (peak SWE, melt timing) via NLDAS-2 orographic forcing across ~15 distinct precip values
Soil-texture control on water partitioning via SSURGO
Peak-SWE validation against SNOTEL (co-located, with expected ridgetop low bias)

not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral routing; independent 1-D columns produce no integrated basin streamflow

not_answerable.aspect: Elevation differences finer than 12 km (sub-cell terrain, within-cell lapse)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 at 0.125 deg has no within-cell lapse rate; columns in the same cell share forcing

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soil), light replication in transition band

classes: dominant coarse (sandy/loamy) SSURGO class per band
dominant fine (clay/silt) SSURGO class per band

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands x 2 dominant soil classes = 8 baseline columns to span the driver crossproduct, plus ~3 replicate columns in the 1000-1500 m rain-snow transition where snow/partitioning is most nonlinear and sensitive. Bands are chosen to fall in distinct NLDAS 12 km cells so the elevation signal is real forcing variation, not just soil.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns along the elevation gradient with extra density in the rain-snow transition band; within each band place on the dominant soil types. Ensure elevation bands map to different NLDAS cells so orographic forcing differs.
sampling_strategy.replication: ~3x in the rain-snow transition band only, because melt timing and partitioning there are most sensitive to small forcing/soil differences.

sampling_plan.reason: Anchors the low-elevation, rain-dominated end of the gradient across coarse and fine dominant soils.
Oversampled band where snow/rain partitioning and melt timing are most nonlinear and sensitive to soil and forcing.
Captures seasonal snow accumulation/melt and partitioning across dominant soils; overlaps SNOTEL elevations.
Represents the high-elevation snow-dominated end; expect ridgetop SWE low bias from 12 km forcing.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place a validation column at each in-domain SNOTEL station; compare simulated peak SWE and melt-out date
validation_design.metric: bias and RMSE of peak SWE; melt-out date offset
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — equals number of in-domain SNOTEL stations (data-dictated)

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — NOT natively supported; would require routing/aggregation of column runoff before any gauge comparison
validation_design.metric: n/a until routing exists (would be NSE / bias)

experiment_summary.validation: pinned to in-domain SNOTEL count (co-located; some may coincide with exploratory snow-band columns)
experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 default forcing, native SSURGO soil, Fan (2013) WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.why: Independent 1-D columns produce no integrated streamflow
NLDAS-2 has no within-cell lapse rate
requires_capabilities.blocks: resolving elevation differences finer than 12 km; reduces ridgetop SWE accuracy

requires_capabilities.why: Needed to pin validation columns to in-domain stations
Assign dominant soil classes per elevation band
Expand elevation bands into concrete points within HUC 17030001
Avoid cold-start artifacts if partitioning/recharge examined
Peak SWE and melt timing needed for SNOTEL comparison

assumptions: Basin is inside CONUS, so NLDAS-2 elevation-resolved forcing applies (verified relief supports ~15 distinct precip values).
Dominant SSURGO soil classes per elevation band will be identified by the downstream expander; exact textures unknown here.
In-domain SNOTEL station count and locations are unknown at design time; validation N follows data density.
Peak-SWE comparison expects ridgetop underestimation from 12 km averaging.
Snow-only interest tolerates a short spin-up; partitioning/recharge interest requires the WTD warm start plus lead time.
open_questions: How many SNOTEL stations lie within HUC 17030001, and at what elevations?
Is basin-integrated streamflow validation required now (would need routing), or is column-scale partitioning sufficient?
Which forcing years/period should be used (full 1980-2018 climatology vs a target window)?
Is recharge/water-table a target here, or is the scope limited to snow and surface partitioning?
